about: Governor contests of 1995, an odd year, in the layout of plan/PLAN.md section 3 with the fields data/README.md adds. Built by pipeline/intake/build_congress.py from Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder (2007-2021), Algara and Amlani's county returns (before, and where Cha lacks a contest), Louisiana's Secretary of State (2023) and New Jersey's and Virginia's certified results (2025), as each contest's source block says. The forecast is the governors' route fitted on the even years before it (data/congress/REPORT.md section 8).

model.what: the model's own forecast (data/congress/REPORT.md section 2), fitted on earlier cycles only, from what was known before the election (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 05:58); no polls are used, so it carries less than forecasters then knew

calibration.note: k = the root mean square of z = (y - mean) / sd over these earlier years' races, each year forecast from its own earlier cycles

model.mean_is: 1/2 + national_forecast + b_lean * lean + b_inc * incumbency + b_lag * (last governor race's Democratic share - 1/2)
model.sd_is: sqrt(national_sd^2 + s_e^2); national_sd = k s_a sqrt(1 + z (Z'Z)^-1 z'), s_e = k s_e_fitted, z = (1, midterm * P, (1 - midterm) * P), P = +1 Democratic president, -1 Republican; k the calibration factor; in an odd year z = (1, w P, 0), w = 1 under the midterm term and 0 under the plain route (odd_year below)

odd_year.note: an odd year: neither the midterm nor the presidential-year term, z = (1, 0, 0) (the plain route; the midterm's term failed the robustness test for odd years, REPORT 8); fitted on the even years before it, never on odd years

variant.note: the mean as fitted, normal tails first (no variant of round 5 passed its test for this level; REPORT 2.7)

near_tie.note: not adopted for this level: on the years it reaches it does not both raise the log score and bring the near-even count nearer (REPORT 2.6)

p.not_computed: Mississippi's governor needed two majorities until the amendment of 2020: the candidate with the most votes in each county or House district was "holden to have received as many votes as such county or district is entitled to members in the House of Representatives, which last named votes are hereby designated 'electoral votes'", and "The person found to have received a majority of all the electoral votes, and also a majority of the popular vote, shall be declared elected"; else "the House of Representatives shall proceed to choose a Governor from the two persons who shall have received the highest number of popular votes" (Constitution of 1890, sections 140 and 141, as the Legislature's House Concurrent Resolution 47 of 2020 prints them, struck and repealed; source ms_hc47_2020). So one vote can decide by crossing the popular majority line or by changing a district's electoral vote, which the tie form does not measure, and p is not computed (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 12:11)
